setting.time_period: Early Victorian England, 1840s, on Christmas Eve and Christmas Day
setting.world: Historical 19th-century England with supernatural ghosts and time-travelling spirits
setting.description: Foggy, snowy Victorian London centered on a gloomy counting-house, Scrooge's dreary chambers in a lowering yard, and small poor homes like the Cratchits' four-roomed house, expanding through spirit visions to a country boarding-school, Fezziwig's warehouse ballroom, bleak moors, miners' huts, a lighthouse, a ship at sea, and churchyards. Streets are lit by gas-lamps and candles, filled with holly, mistletoe, poulterers' and grocers' displays, bakers' shops, and horse-drawn carriages in biting cold.

characters.name: Ebenezer Scrooge
characters.physical_description: An old man with a pointed nose, shrivelled cheek, red eyes, thin blue lips, and a stiff gait. He has frosty white rime on his head, eyebrows, and wiry chin, and typically wears a greatcoat buttoned to the chin, cravat, dressing gown, slippers, and nightcap indoors.

characters.name: Jacob Marley
characters.physical_description: A transparent phantom with a livid face, wide motionless eyes, ghostly spectacles turned up on his forehead, and hair curiously stirred. He wears a pigtail, usual waistcoat, tights and tasseled boots, a folded kerchief bound about head and chin, and a long chain wound about him made of cash-boxes, keys, padlocks, ledgers, deeds and steel purses.

characters.name: Bob Cratchit
characters.physical_description: An adult man in threadbare clothes darned up to look seasonable, with at least three feet of white comforter hanging down before him. He wears no greatcoat and carries his threadbare attire brushed for Christmas.

characters.name: Tiny Tim
characters.physical_description: A very small young crippled boy with withered limbs supported by an iron frame. He bears a little crutch and sits on a little stool beside the fire.

characters.name: Mrs. Cratchit
characters.physical_description: A motherly woman dressed poorly in a twice-turned gown. She is brave in cheap ribbons and wears a shawl and bonnet when out.

characters.name: Peter Cratchit
characters.physical_description: A boy wearing a monstrous shirt-collar, his father's private property conferred for the day, which nearly chokes him. He has a youthful face often seen looking thoughtfully at the fire from between his collars.

characters.name: Martha Cratchit
characters.physical_description: A young girl in a shawl and bonnet, dressed as a poor milliner's apprentice. She has a youthful face and plain working clothes.

characters.name: Belinda Cratchit
characters.physical_description: A young girl brave in ribbons like her mother, in a poor but festive dress. She has a youthful face and helps serve the family dinner.

characters.name: Fred
characters.physical_description: A young man all in a glow from rapid walking, with a ruddy handsome face, sparkling eyes, and smoking breath in the cold. He wears winter outer clothes for fog and frost.

characters.name: Scrooge's niece
characters.physical_description: An exceedingly pretty young woman with a dimpled, surprised-looking face, ripe little mouth, and the sunniest pair of eyes. She wears a festive dress and sits with a footstool in a snug corner.

characters.name: Ghost of Christmas Past
characters.physical_description: A strange diminutive figure like a child yet like an old man, with white hair hanging about neck and down back, unwrinkled blooming skin, very long muscular bare arms and delicately formed bare legs and feet. It wears a tunic of purest white with a lustrous belt, summer flowers trimming, holds a branch of fresh green holly, and bears a bright clear jet of light springing from its crown with a grea

characters.name: Ghost of Christmas Present
characters.physical_description: A jolly giant with dark-brown long free curls, sparkling eyes, and genial open face, clothed in a simple deep green robe bordered with white fur leaving his capacious breast and feet bare. He wears a holly wreath set with shining icicles on his head, an antique rust-eaten scabbard with no sword about his middle, and bears a glowing torch shaped like Plenty's horn.

characters.name: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come
characters.physical_description: A tall stately figure entirely shrouded in a deep black garment concealing head, face, and form. Nothing is visible of it save one outstretched hand.

characters.name: Old Fezziwig
characters.physical_description: A stout old gentleman in a Welsh wig behind a high desk, with a capacious waistcoat. He is large, jovial in appearance with a comfortable, oily, rich appearance from shoes to head.

characters.name: Mrs. Fezziwig
characters.physical_description: A stout middle-aged woman with one vast substantial smile. She wears a festive ball dress for the Christmas dance.

characters.name: Dick Wilkins
characters.physical_description: A young man and fellow apprentice, brisk in movement. He wears early 19th-century apprentice work clothes.

characters.name: Fan
characters.physical_description: A little girl much younger than her brother, tiny with a childish eager face. She wears a child's winter dress and comes darting in with joy.

characters.name: Belle
characters.physical_description: A fair young girl in a mourning dress, beautiful with tear-sparkling eyes.

characters.name: Topper
characters.physical_description: A young bachelor gentleman in evening party dress. He is an ordinary young man with a plain face that can growl in bass singing.

characters.name: Old Joe
characters.physical_description: A grey-haired rascal nearly seventy years of age, screened by a curtaining of miscellaneous tatters. He smokes a pipe by a charcoal stove made of old bricks in a shop of rags and iron.

characters.name: Mrs. Dilber
characters.physical_description: A middle-aged working woman in plain worn clothes carrying a heavy bundle of laundry. She has a bold, plain face and workwoman's attire.

characters.name: Caroline
characters.physical_description: A young mild and patient mother in a poor but tidy day dress. She has an anxious face and works with her needle while waiting.

characters.name: Ignorance
characters.physical_description: A wretched yellow meagre ragged boy, wolfish and scowling, pinched and twisted like age. He kneels in rags clinging to the Spirit's robe.

characters.name: Want
characters.physical_description: A wretched yellow meagre ragged girl, wolfish and scowling, pinched and twisted like age. She kneels in rags clinging to the Spirit's robe.

chapters.title: Marley’s Ghost
chapters.summary: On Christmas Eve miserly Ebenezer Scrooge rejects his nephew, charity collectors, and his clerk's holiday spirit. Returning to his gloomy chambers, he is confronted by the chained transparent ghost of his dead partner Jacob Marley. Marley warns that Scrooge forges a similar chain and will be haunted by Three Spirits to offer a chance of escape.
chapters.cover_description: Transparent ghost of Jacob Marley bound in a long steel chain of cash-boxes, keys, padlocks and ledgers, confronting miserly Scrooge in nightcap and dressing gown before a low fire in a gloomy Victorian sitting room at night.

chapters.title: The First of the Three Spirits
chapters.summary: Scrooge is visited at one o'clock by the Ghost of Christmas Past, who takes him through the wall to revisit his lonely boyhood, Fan's rescue, merry apprenticeship at Fezziwig's ball, and his broken engagement to Belle over gain. Forced to witness Belle's happy family and his own solitary fate while his partner lay dying, Scrooge begs for release and crushes the Spirit's light with its extinguisher-cap, collapsing into heavy sleep in his own bedroom.
chapters.cover_description: The diminutive Ghost of Christmas Past glowing with a bright jet of light from its crown, in a white tunic trimmed with summer flowers and holding holly, confronting a nightcapped Ebenezer Scrooge in his dark curtained four-poster bedroom.

chapters.title: The Second of the Three Spirits
chapters.summary: The Ghost of Christmas Present, a jolly giant with a glowing torch, takes Scrooge through Christmas morning in London, blessing poor dinners and rebuking Scrooge's Sabbatarian cant. They share the Cratchits' humble goose and pudding feast where the Spirit foretells Tiny Tim's death, then rove to miners, lighthouse keepers, sailors, and Fred's merry party where Scrooge is laughed at yet pitied and toasted. As midnight nears the Spirit ages and reveals two wretched children, Ignorance and Want, wa
chapters.cover_description: A jolly giant spirit with long dark curls and a holly wreath crowned with icicles, wearing a deep green robe bordered with white fur, holding a glowing torch like Plenty's horn aloft while enthroned on a mountain of Christmas feast — turkeys, geese, puddings, fruit and punch — in a room transformed into a living green grove of holly, mistletoe and ivy with a roaring fire.

chapters.title: The Last of the Spirits
chapters.summary: The silent Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come shows Scrooge a future where an unloved dead man is mocked on 'Change, robbed by servants and Old Joe, and mourned by no one except with relief by his debtors. Scrooge then sees the Cratchits grieving Tiny Tim, discovers his own neglected grave, and begs to change his course, vowing to honour Christmas in Past, Present and Future.
chapters.cover_description: Ebenezer Scrooge on his knees in a choked, weed-overrun churchyard at night, clutching the black robe of the tall shrouded Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come as its skeletal hand points down to a neglected gravestone reading EBENEZER SCROOGE.

chapters.title: The End of It
chapters.summary: Waking on Christmas morning to find he has not missed the day, Scrooge rejoices that the shadows may be dispelled and vows to keep Past, Present and Future in his heart. He sends the prize turkey to the Cratchits, makes amends with a grand charity donation, joins Fred's dinner in joyful welcome, and the next morning raises Bob's salary, becoming a good master, generous friend, and second father to Tiny Tim ever after.
chapters.cover_description: Ebenezer Scrooge flinging open his bedroom window on a bright, clear Christmas morning, laughing and crying with joy in his dressing gown and nightcap as church bells ring and golden sunlight floods the cold winter street below.
